questions.question:
The number of \(3-\)digit numbers, that are divisible by either \(2\) or \(3\) but not divisible by \(7\) is

 

[JEE Main 2023, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
First count the three-digit numbers divisible by \(2\) or \(3\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(2\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{2}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{2}\right\rfloor=499-49=450\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(3\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{3}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{3}\right\rfloor=333-33=300\)

The numbers counted in both groups are the multiples of \(6\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(6\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{6}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{6}\right\rfloor=166-16=150\)

Therefore, the number divisible by \(2\) or \(3\) is \(450+300-150=600\)

Now remove the numbers that are also divisible by \(7\)

A number divisible by \(7\) and \(2\) is divisible by \(14\)

and a number divisible by \(7\) and \(3\) is divisible by \(21\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(14\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{14}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{14}\right\rfloor=71-7=64\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(21\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{21}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{21}\right\rfloor=47-4=43\)

The numbers counted in both of these groups are the multiples of \(42\)

The number of three-digit multiples of \(42\) is

\(\left\lfloor\dfrac{999}{42}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\dfrac{99}{42}\right\rfloor=23-2=21\)

Hence, the number divisible by \(7\) and also by \(2\) or \(3\) is \(64+43-21=86\)

Therefore, the required number is \(600-86=514\)
